clue.text: Regulator mishandled hot matters

indicators.note: something mishandled has been treated roughly and put out of its proper order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An official regulator has bungled some heated, controversial business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulator' reads like a watchdog body, but here it is a device; THERMOSTAT is the rearranged letters of 'hot matters', which fits nicely since it controls heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is a device that automatically keeps a heating system at a set temperature, so it literally regulates.

clue.text: Briefly stroke an exotic bird

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: touch, a light stroke, without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives a quick pat to a colourful tropical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUCH loses its H, then AN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a big-billed tropical American species, so it counts as an exotic bird to a British solver.

clue.text: Replica I'm changing based on experience

indicators.note: letters that are changing are moving into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A copy of something says it is improving through practical experience.
explanation.walkthrough: All nine letters of 'Replica I'm' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge comes from observation and practical trial rather than theory or pure logic.

clue.text: Make attractive image sent all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flattering picture is circulated widely to make someone look appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make attractive' suggests glamour, but the sense is physical: giving something magnetic pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnetise an iron object is to give it the power to pull metals towards it, a literal kind of attraction.

clue.text: Somewhat prudish if they move

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only a part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the next two

explanation.surface: People are a bit squeamish about what happens if they relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside prudiSH IF They.
explanation.definitionFit: Shift and move are synonyms as verbs: both mean to change position or place.

clue.text: No actress goes off those who came before

indicators.note: food that goes off has spoiled, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: No performer walks out on the stars who preceded her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' looks like an exit from the stage, but it signals rearrangement of 'no actress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestors are the forebears in a family line, people who lived earlier in time.

clue.text: Parking, admitted to wrong turn

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver confesses to parking after taking a wrong turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong turn' reads as a mistake in driving; 'wrong' gives SIN and 'turn' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to rotate, and a spin is a whirl or revolution, so it matches turn.

clue.text: Hearing of quiet composition

indicators.note: hearing a word means taking it by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: peace is quiet; the two words sound identical

explanation.surface: A first performance of a hushed musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a concert listening, but it tells you to go by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece is a single work or composition, as in a piano piece.

clue.text: Answer stops short, possibly? Don't mention it

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one item fills a space inside another

parts.note: someone short is perhaps not tall
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A reply falls short of the mark, perhaps, but the speaker brushes it aside.
explanation.walkthrough: A plugs the gap in NOT TALL; 'possibly' admits that not tall is only one way of being short.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are polite conversational replies to thanks, waving away any need for gratitude.

clue.text: Fine Greek character's cheese

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A splendid Greek person owns some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek cheese made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Perhaps remove from line in a French page, say

parts.note: un is French for a
P is the abbreviation for page
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike a line from a French page, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests text, but the definition means a washing line; 'Perhaps' marks taking clothes off it as one example of unpegging.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg laundry is to take out the clothes pegs holding it, freeing it from the washing line.

clue.text: Addition of popular setter inspiring resistance

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one thing is drawn inside another

parts.note: cement is something that sets hard
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A well-liked crossword compiler adds a touch of defiance to the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you towards ME, the crossword setter, but here it is a substance that sets: CEMENT, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase or added amount, one step of growth, so it is an addition.

clue.text: Concur concerning boring period

indicators.note: something boring drills through and ends up lodged within

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Everyone accepts that a particular era is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as tedious, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, which is exactly what agreeing means.

clue.text: Will try a time to ring blokes

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the outer letters go around

parts.note: to test is to try out
taken as written
blokes is British slang for men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone called Will attempts to find a moment to phone some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name at the start of a sentence; it is the definition. A and T wrap around MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out what happens to someone's estate after death.

clue.text: City fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A city that used to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits cleanly after its first word, with two plain synonyms following in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large American metropolis on Lake Michigan in Illinois.

clue.text: Love helping to support American party

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the first piece goes below the rest

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a do is an informal party
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Affection that comes from assisting a US political party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to support' puts one piece underneath the other, so the helping sits below A DO. 'Party' suggests politics but means a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, a strong form of the same feeling.

clue.text: Complete child extremely asocial

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of the word

explanation.surface: A child who is utterly unsociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'asocial', but it takes its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and complete are synonyms as adjectives, both meaning whole or absolute, as in total silence.

clue.text: Distressed, ditch love in theatre

indicators.note: distressed means battered or agitated, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Upset, someone dumps their partner during a play.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OLD VIC is a famous theatre in London, near Waterloo station.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Vic is a historic London playhouse, so it is a specific example of a theatre.

clue.text: Vigorous martial arts star Jackie in Midlands river

indicators.note: something in a place is inside it

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
Jackie Chan is the Hong Kong action film star

explanation.surface: An energetic kung-fu film star wades into an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent flows through Nottingham and Stoke in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means forceful and incisive, as in trenchant criticism, so it fits vigorous in the sense of strong.

clue.text: Soldier's small fruit from India eaten finally

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each word, so only last letters are kept

parts.note: the last letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A soldier's little bit of Indian fruit has been eaten up at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word, but it supplies the M; 'India' tempts you to use the NATO letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearman is a warrior armed with a spear, a kind of foot soldier from earlier times.

clue.text: Beat up around London School of Economics

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the usual initials of the London university college

explanation.surface: Someone is assaulted near a London university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat up' reads as one phrase meaning assault; split it, with 'Beat' the definition and 'up' turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the regular throb of the heart felt at the wrist, a rhythmic beat.

clue.text: Horrible part of play following introduction of orthodox bishop

indicators.note: following means coming after, which fixes the order of the joined pieces
an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
B is the chess notation for bishop
a scene is a division of a play

explanation.surface: A section of a drama, coming after a conservative cleric appears, is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the scene after the O and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene can mean offensive or repugnant, as in obscene wealth, which matches horrible in an informal sense.

clue.text: Rented meadows on outskirts of Enfield

parts.note: leas are meadows, a poetic word

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outside letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Some grassland on the edge of a north London suburb is let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Enfield is a borough on the northern fringe of London, which suits 'outskirts' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to rent it under a contract, so leased and rented are synonyms.

clue.text: One who helps when little sister cheers, not lacking heart

indicators.note: to lack a heart is to have the middle missing, so the central letter is dropped

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
sis is a short form of sister
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
the word with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: A kind helper steps in when a younger sibling is cheering without much spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and 'ta' are both casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone employed or volunteering to aid another person, a helper by definition.

clue.text: Country star probed by District Attorney

indicators.note: something probed has an instrument pushed into it

parts.note: the sun is a star
DA is the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A country music celebrity is investigated by a prosecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country star' reads as a singer; split it, with 'Country' the definition and 'star' the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa, south of Egypt.

clue.text: Regularly, she falls for marine mammal

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A woman keeps falling in love with a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls for' reads as falling in love, but 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals are flippered sea creatures that breathe air and suckle young, hence mammals living in the ocean.

clue.text: Sorted out pitch with minor bit of damage holding United up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
to hold something is to keep it inside your grasp

parts.note: a dent is slight damage to a surface
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football ground was repaired with a small damaged patch keeping Manchester United's game on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field but belongs to the definition, the musical sense. DENT holds U, and the whole reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuned instrument has had its notes adjusted to the correct musical frequency.

clue.text: Liberal old English barrister, revolutionary philosopher

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a revolution is a turn right round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a KC, King's Counsel, is a senior barrister

explanation.surface: A former radical English lawyer of liberal views became an influential thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: KC stands for King's Counsel, a senior British barrister; E and KC together are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the seventeenth-century English thinker behind liberal political theory and empiricism.

clue.text: Resolving disputes, Charlie quits drugs?

indicators.note: someone who quits leaves, so that letter departs

parts.note: medication is drugs, the question mark flagging the loose fit
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: In settling arguments, a man named Charlie gives up narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is also slang for cocaine, which the surface plays on; here it is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is the process of a neutral third party helping opponents settle a quarrel.

clue.text: Bottles six beers, not European

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is left out

parts.note: ales are beers
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone downs half a dozen beers, though not continental ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as a verb about drinking; it is the noun definition. ALES drops its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small glass containers for liquids such as medicine, so they are little bottles.

clue.text: Bolshevik leader heading west, ignoring large number

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftwards, so the word is read backwards
to ignore something is to leave it out

parts.note: Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A revolutionary chief travels west, disregarding a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large number' reads as a phrase; split it, since 'number' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, the integer between eight and ten.

clue.text: Ignorant, you ultimately want to pinch old coin

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between finger and thumb, gripping something inside

parts.note: to want is to need
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe

explanation.surface: Uninformed, you eventually feel the urge to steal an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' suggests stealing, but here it means gripping, so NEED wraps the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uneducated lacks schooling or knowledge, which is what ignorant means.
